correctness.rationale: The theorem specifies a uniform k-subset of n primary species, partner sizes a,b and overlap c. One-step change c->c+1 replaces one B-exclusive species y by one A-exclusive x. Pairing samples in which exactly one of x,y survives yields exactly one four-point mixed difference of phi, with binomial coefficients for the c common, a-c-1 A-only, b-c-1 B-only and n-a-b+c outside regions. Each weight is nonnegative, proving full supermodular order over all feasible c and 0<=k<=n; each marginal is independently hypergeometric. Applying phi=1_{i>=r}1_{j>=s} gives the exact quorum increment and strictness condition. Inclusion-exclusion yields covariance [C(n-a-b+c,k)C(n,k)-C(n-a,k)C(n-b,k)]/C(n,k)^2 and Pascal monotonic increments. At (n,k,a,b)=(7,3,3,3), numerators -16,-16,19,124 over 1225 confirm sign transition. Independent direct enumeration checked 8,682 n<=7 threshold identities including boundaries, source verifier covers parameters n<=9. General proof, not finite testing, establishes all n.
